Only methods declared in sugar-toast/src, or inherited from a parent declared there, are listed. A type that extends a class outside that tree, such as \RuntimeException, does not show the methods of that class.

Alert final class

A single alert entry in the queue.

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly ToastType $type, public readonly ?string $message = null, public readonly ?float $expiresAt = null, public readonly ?float $progress = null, public readonly array $actions = [], public readonly ?Color $backgroundColor = null, public readonly ?Color $foregroundColor = null, public readonly ?Color $borderColor = null, public readonly bool $persistent = false, public readonly ?string $id = null, public readonly ?AlertTypeDefinition $definition = null, public readonly ?float $ttl = null)
static new(ToastType $type, ?string $message = null, ?float $expiresAt = null, ?float $progress = null, array $actions = [], ?Color $backgroundColor = null, ?Color $foregroundColor = null, ?Color $borderColor = null, bool $persistent = false, ?string $id = null, ?AlertTypeDefinition $definition = null, ?float $ttl = null): selfFactory mirroring Action::new() / Toast::new() — Alert once had only the bare ctor while its siblings led with ::new(). Arguments and defaults mirror the constructor exactly; the remaining fields ride through mutate() so the full positional transcription lives in exactly one place (the mutate() call itself).
isExpired(): boolExpiry reads CLOCK_REALTIME (microtime) — an NTP step can shorten or lengthen how long a live alert stays on screen. A monotonic-clock injection seam is a recorded future API candidate; no rate assumption here is load-bearing beyond display timing.
withoutExpiry(): selfDEPRECATED forwarder to withCancelledExpiry() — the two spellings were one door all along, and the twin doubled API surface, census rows, and greppability in a lib whose naming culture renamed getHistory → history outright. withCancelledExpiry() is the canonical spelling (the sentinel's own vocabulary); this alias stays callable until 2.x so existing hosts keep compiling. The sentinel once did not exist at all, and push() re-inherited an expiry precisely because no state distinguished "never" from "not stated" — the history the alias name froze.
withCancelledExpiry(): selfCanonical persistence door: set the persistent sentinel + clear the expiry (used by Toast::cancelAlert()).
withExtendedExpiry(float $additionalSeconds): selfRe-arm the expiry: the alert now expires $additionalSeconds from NOW. This is a reset, not a push-back — extending an alert that still has 30 s left by 5 s leaves it with 5 s, the behaviour a pointer-hover re-show wants. Clears persistence alongside (a timer was asked for).
withExpiry(float $duration): selfExpire $duration seconds from NOW (the clock starts at this call). Clears persistence and any pending withTtl() lifetime.
withTtl(float $seconds): selfGive the alert a relative lifetime that starts when it is QUEUED: Alert::new(ToastType::Error, $msg)->withTtl(3.0) shows for three seconds from the moment Toast::push() takes it, however long the alert waited before. Unlike withExpiry() (which starts the clock now), nothing is armed yet, so the alert is not expired until pushed. Clears any absolute expiry and the persistent sentinel, and overrides the toast's withDuration() default.
withProgress(float $progress): selfAttach a progress value (0.0–1.0). Finite out-of-range values are clamped; non-finite values are refused (see the constructor law).
withActions(array $actions): selfAttach action buttons.
withBackgroundColor(?Color $color): selfSet the box background-fill colour (null clears it → plain render).
withForegroundColor(?Color $color): selfSet the message-text (foreground) colour (null = terminal default).
withBorderColor(?Color $color): selfSet the box-glyph (border) colour (null = terminal default).

AlertTypeRegistry final class

Immutable registry of custom alert types — the registration seam bubbleup exposes as RegisterNewAlertType, made a value the host hands to Toast::withTypeRegistry() instead of process-global mutable state (every Toast here is immutable; a package-level registry would let two hosts in one process stomp each other's types).

Toast final class

Floating alert notification renderer.

MethodSummary
__construct(int $maxWidth = 50)
static new(int $maxWidth = 50): self
withMaxWidth(int $w): self
withMinWidth(int $w): selfMinimum box width in cells — a MASTER SWITCH, not just a floor: 0 (default) keeps the box FIXED at full width (maxWidth, capped by the frame); ANY positive value engages fit-content sizing, where the box shrinks toward its message between this floor and maxWidth. A caller setting withMinWidth(20) "to allow narrow alerts" flips the whole width model — that is the switch engaging, not a side effect.
withPosition(Position $pos): self
withSymbolSet(SymbolSet $set): self
withDuration(?float $seconds): selfAuto-dismiss alerts after $duration seconds. Pass null to disable auto-dismiss.
withTypeRegistry(?AlertTypeRegistry $registry): selfRegister custom alert types (bubbleup's RegisterNewAlertType, as a value). String types passed to alert()/progressToast() then resolve registry-first and fall back to the four built-ins, so a registered deploy type paints its own prefix/colour while an unregistered unknown string still throws.
withAllowEscToClose(bool $allow): selfSet the allowEscToClose preference flag.
withAccessibleText(bool $on = true): selfOpt into a text channel for information the frame otherwise carries ONLY as colour, glyph, or block-run length: the severity word (Warning, Error, … via ToastType::label(), so it follows the active locale) joins the header, and progress rows print the numeric percentage beside the bar. Default OFF — the plain renderer's byte output is unchanged for every existing host.
withHostZoneCarry(bool $on = true): selfOpt in/out of carrying host zone markers through the composite.
accessibleText(): boolReturns the accessible-text preference flag (see withAccessibleText()).
allowEscToClose(): boolReturns the allowEscToClose preference flag.
withMaxConcurrent(?int $max): selfSet the maximum number of concurrent alerts. Pass null for unlimited.
withOverflow(Overflow $overflow): selfSet the overflow strategy when maxConcurrent is exceeded.
withHistoryLimit(?int $limit): selfCap the history log at $limit entries, evicting the oldest first (the Overflow::DropOldest policy applied to history). The default is 100; pass null to keep every dismissed alert unbounded.
alert(ToastType|string $type, string $message, ?float $expiresAt = null, ?array $actions = null, ?string $id = null, ?float $ttlSeconds = null): selfAdd an alert to the queue. Returns a new Toast instance.
progressToast(ToastType|string $type, string $message, float $progress, ?float $expiresAt = null, ?array $actions = null, ?string $id = null, ?float $ttlSeconds = null): selfAdd a progress toast — renders a progress bar beneath the message.
push(Alert $alert): selfEnqueue a pre-built (optionally styled) Alert.
error(string $message, ?float $expiresAt = null, ?array $actions = null, ?string $id = null, ?float $ttlSeconds = null): selfConvenience: show an error alert. Carries the full alert() tail ($expiresAt/$actions/$id/$ttlSeconds, delegated verbatim) — a shortcut once took only the message, so extra positional arguments were silently dropped by PHP: the buttons and id a caller believed attached existed nowhere.
warning(string $message, ?float $expiresAt = null, ?array $actions = null, ?string $id = null, ?float $ttlSeconds = null): selfConvenience: show a warning alert (full alert() tail, see error()).
info(string $message, ?float $expiresAt = null, ?array $actions = null, ?string $id = null, ?float $ttlSeconds = null): selfConvenience: show an info alert (full alert() tail, see error()).
success(string $message, ?float $expiresAt = null, ?array $actions = null, ?string $id = null, ?float $ttlSeconds = null): selfConvenience: show a success alert (full alert() tail, see error()).
dismiss(): selfStop rendering and file EVERY queued alert into the history log.
pruneExpired(): selfRemove expired alerts and return a new Toast.
clear(): selfClear the entire queue and reset the dismissed flag, resuming rendering — the documented revival path after dismiss().
removeAlert(string $id): selfRemove the queued alert carrying $id (first match), WITHOUT recording it in history — this is the lifecycle door for updates and cancellations the host performs deliberately (a finished download's progress box disappearing is not a dismissal). The companion of the replace-by-id leg in appendBounded(): before it existed, the only way to retire an alert before expiry was dismiss(), which nukes the whole queue and files every survivor under history).
cancelAlert(int $index): selfCancel the expiry on the alert at $index, making it persistent — $index addresses activeAlerts() (the live queue, not the raw array), and the change goes through the explicit sentinel Alert::withCancelledExpiry(). Has no effect if $index is out of bounds or the alert is already persistent.
extendAlert(int $index, float $additionalSeconds): selfRe-arm the auto-dismiss timer on the alert at $index (a activeAlerts() index — the live queue) to $additionalSeconds from now. This is a reset, not a push-back: extending an alert that still has 30 s left by 5 s leaves it with 5 s. Has no effect if $index is out of bounds or the alert never expires — a persistent alert has no timer to extend (mirrors extendAll()).
extendAll(float $additionalSeconds): selfRe-arm the auto-dismiss timer on every expiring alert to $additionalSeconds from now (a reset — see extendAlert()). Only affects alerts that have an expiry; non-expiring alerts are unchanged.
hasActiveAlert(): boolReturns true if there are active (non-expired) alerts in the queue.
nextExpiry(): ?floatThe soonest expiry instant (seconds since epoch) among the queued alerts that auto-dismiss, or null when no queued alert has an expiry.
secondsUntilNextExpiry(): ?floatSeconds from now until the next alert expires, clamped to >= 0.0 (an already-due alert yields 0.0 → prune now), or null when no queued alert auto-dismisses. Convenience for scheduling a single prune tick, e.g. Cmd::tick($toast->secondsUntilNextExpiry() ?? $idle, …).
tickCmd(): ?\ClosureThe command that wakes the host when the next live alert expires, or null when nothing is waiting to expire (no live alert auto-dismisses, every timed alert has already expired, or the toast is dismissed).
history(): arrayReturn the history of dismissed alerts.
view(string $background, int $viewportWidth = 80, int $viewportHeight = 24): stringRender the toast layer composited over a background view using Buffer-based composition.
compositeInto(Buffer $buffer): BufferPaint the toast layer into a host's cell buffer and return the result.
withActionsExpanded(int $alertIndex, bool $on = true): selfExpand (or collapse) one alert's [+N more] action fold: the alert then shows up to MAX_EXPANDED_ACTIONS buttons and every one is a hit rect. $alertIndex addresses activeAlerts() like cancelAlert(); out of range is a no-op returning the same instance. The keyboard-driven twin of expandAt().
expandAt(int $col, int $row, ?string $background = null, ?int $viewportWidth = null, ?int $viewportHeight = null): ?selfThe mouse door for the fold: when ($col, $row) lies on a painted [+N more] row, the Toast with that alert expanded; null anywhere else. Hosts do $next = $toast->expandAt($c, $r); if ($next !== null) { $toast = $next; } beside their actionAt() dispatch. Same frame-args contract as actionAt().
activeAlerts(): arrayThe live queue exactly as view() sees it: queue order, expired alerts filtered: before this accessor existed, cancelAlert() and extendAlert() indexed a RAW queue the host could not observe, so a stale expired entry silently shifted every later index.
actionRects(?string $background = null, ?int $viewportWidth = null, ?int $viewportHeight = null): arrayHit-test rectangles for every rendered action button, in the same coordinate system view() composites in (absolute frame rows / columns, 0-based). The layout is RECOMPUTED from the arguments given — there is no saved last-frame — over a frame of max(background lines, viewportHeight, total stack height): a host that painted with a non-empty $background must pass the same three arguments here, or the default ''/80/24 assumes a shorter frame and every bottom/middle row shifts out of register with the screen. Zone-neutral by design: sugar-toast carries no sugar-mouse dependency and forges no zone sentinels — hosts map their own mouse events through actionAt() (or drive keyboards from this same surface) and invoke the returned Action's callback themselves.
frame(?string $background = null, ?int $viewportWidth = null, ?int $viewportHeight = null): ?ToastFrameThe frame currently on screen (or the one the arguments describe) as a ToastFrame: composed bytes, top-box origin, and hit rects as data. null when nothing renders. Optional arguments resolve against the last render's memo exactly like actionRects().
actionAt(int $col, int $row, ?string $background = null, ?int $viewportWidth = null, ?int $viewportHeight = null): ?ActionWhich Action (if any) covers frame position ($col, $row) of the frame the host is looking at? Omitted arguments read the last-rendered frame; supplied ones that differ from it throw (see actionRects()). Where two boxes share rows, the top-most (newest) one wins — the visible button is the hittable one. This is the dispatch door the README's host-side mouse/keyboard recipe calls.

ToastFrame final class

A rendered frame: the exact bytes Toast::view() painted, plus the geometry that produced them.

MethodSummary
__construct(public readonly int $x, public readonly int $y, public readonly string $rows, public readonly array $rects = [], public readonly ?array $bounds = null)
boxRows(): arrayThe composed frame as a list of lines, without the trailing-newline artefact. Over an empty background these are exactly the box rows: dashboard-style consumers stop splitting and trimming rendered ANSI.
actionRects(): arrayAbsolute frame cells of every painted action button — the same structure actionAt() walks.
actionAt(int $col, int $row): ?ActionWhich Action (if any) covers frame position ($col, $row)? Where boxes share rows, the top-most (newest) one wins — walking in reverse paint order, because a later box is composited OVER an earlier one and a button hidden beneath it must never fire.
placeAt(int $col, int $row): selfRe-anchor the painted boxes at a host-chosen cell: the inset door the nine anchors cannot express (candy-code wants a top-right box inset from the screen edge, and hand-pasted rows with a re-derived x).
foldAt(int $col, int $row): ?intThe activeAlerts() index whose [+N more] fold row covers frame position ($col, $row), or null. Fold rects ride actionRects() flagged by a non-zero 'fold' (the hidden-button count) but never answer actionAt() — hosts invoking the returned Action's callback must not mistake the fold for a button; this is its own door.
